issues: When event.image_url is empty, is rendered with src="" (via mediaUrl('')) — Chrome logs a warning 'An empty string was passed to the src attribute'. Not user-visible but noisy. Fix: skip the or pass a placeholder when image_url is falsy.

action_items: Cosmetic: don't render in EventCard when image_url is empty (see mediaUrl usage) to eliminate the console warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 1068 lines — still >700 line threshold. Splitting into routers (auth, friends, events, admin, notifications, push, digest, reminders) is overdue.

serialize_event() runs O(events × interests × user-lookups) per /events call — friend user lookups inside the inner loop repeat across events. For 6 seeded events it's fine, but consider batching: fetch all interested user docs in one $in query, keyed by id.

mutual_friends_count() is called per-user in /users/search and /friends/requests, each doing its own accepted_friend_ids() (2 queries per candidate). For 20 search results that's ~40 extra Mongo round-trips. Preload all my friends once (already done) and batch other_ids similarly, or cache.

generate_event_reminders() dedup relies on a filter 'data.event_id': ev['id']; if create_notification is later refactored to change the data schema, dedup silently breaks. Consider a unique compound index on (user_id, type, data.event_id) with sparse.
EventCard passes mediaUrl(event.image_url) which produces '' when input is '' — causes browser warning; also the then triggers a whole-page refetch per React's warning.

Feed.js deep-link useEffect depends on [events] only, so if the ?event param is present on first mount before events load, it fires correctly; but if the user changes filters while the param is still in the URL (edge case), the effect re-runs and re-scrolls. Minor.

Server time is UTC but generate_event_reminders() uses Europe/Madrid on the event start — good. However date_in_filter uses UTC 'today' — during Palma late-night hours between 00:00 and 02:00 local, 'hoy'/'all' may show yesterday's events as past (or hide them for a couple of hours). Consider using PALMA_TZ for date_in_filter too for consistency.
